checklist.name: delayed umbilical cord separation

quotes.text: delayed separation of the umbilical cord and dramatically impaired or dysregulated wound healing in LAD-I

checklist.why: Classic neonatal sign and a clinical criterion for severe LAD-I.

checklist.name: omphalitis

quotes.text: Omphalitis was considered the most frequent symptom in patients aged <6 months
Umbilical cord related complications like omphalitis (64%)

checklist.why: Most frequent early manifestation in severe disease.

checklist.name: leukocytosis or neutrophilia

quotes.text: Persistent neutrophilic leukocytosis was the characteristic finding in all patients
basal and persistent neutrophilia in the absence of obvious infection

checklist.why: Hallmark laboratory finding, routinely reported with counts.

checklist.name: absence of pus formation

quotes.text: The absence of pus and persistent marked neutrophilic leukocytosis are the hallmarks of LAD
a defect in formation of pus

checklist.why: Hallmark sign that papers state as present or absent.

checklist.name: skin or soft tissue infections

quotes.text: omphalitis, skin and soft tissue infections, delayed umbilical cord detachment
the most common symptoms to be umbilical cord complications, skin infections

checklist.why: Among the commonest infections at all ages.

checklist.name: necrotic skin ulcers or pyoderma gangrenosum-like lesions

quotes.text: Necrotic skin ulcer was the most common infection in LAD1^+ which may mimic pyoderma gangrenosum
recurrent skin lesions like pyoderma gangrenosum

checklist.why: Commonest manifestation of the milder, later-presenting phenotype.

checklist.name: impaired wound healing

quotes.text: impaired or dysplastic remodeling of infected sites and wounds

checklist.why: Characteristic of LAD-I, especially moderate disease.

checklist.name: periodontitis or gingivitis

quotes.text: Periodontal infections including gingivitis and oral ulcers

checklist.why: Typical chronic complication in survivors and moderate disease.

checklist.name: tooth loss
checklist.why: Named consequence in moderate LAD-I; distinct from the gum inflammation itself.

checklist.name: lower respiratory tract infection
checklist.why: One of the commonest infections in cohorts.

checklist.name: otitis media

quotes.text: delayed umbilical cord detachment, otitis media, and sepsis

checklist.why: Common early presenting infection in the Indian cohort.

checklist.name: sepsis

quotes.text: may ultimately lead to sepsis and organ damage

checklist.why: Frequent life-threatening infection.

checklist.name: meningitis
checklist.why: Serious CNS infection tabulated in the cohort.

checklist.name: gastrointestinal infections
checklist.why: Named by the Delphi panel among common manifestations after 6 months.

checklist.name: colitis or gastrointestinal inflammatory disease
checklist.why: Inflammatory complication driven by IL-23/IL-17 dysregulation.

checklist.name: diarrhea
checklist.why: Symptom tabulated per subtype in the cohort.

checklist.name: fungal infections

quotes.text: fungal infections were noted in 7 patient

checklist.why: Organism class that case reports name explicitly.

checklist.name: bcg vaccine complications
checklist.why: Named as a sign raising clinical suspicion.

checklist.name: failure to thrive
checklist.why: Growth outcome tabulated in about a third of severe cases.

checklist.name: autoimmune complications

quotes.text: Late- onset autoimmune complications have been reported previously

checklist.why: Late-onset complication in long-term survivors.

left_out: perianal infection: a site of skin/soft tissue infection, so it would sit inside item 5
oral ulcers: 33391282 groups them under periodontal infections
inflammatory skin disease: overlaps necrotic skin ulcers / pyoderma gangrenosum-like lesions
recurrent, severe or life-threatening infections; bacterial infections: too broad, would contain the site-specific infection items
respiratory tract infections in general: split into lower respiratory tract infection and otitis media to avoid nesting
umbilical cord complications: covered by delayed separation and omphalitis
consanguinity and family history: not phenotypes
reduced CD18/CD11 expression: defines the disease
bleeding tendency, anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, osteopetrosis: LAD-III features, not LAD-I
mental and growth retardation, Bombay phenotype: LAD-II features
death, graft failure, GvHD, ICU admission: outcomes or treatment events
notes: Written from three sources by the coordinator's instruction (the Delphi consensus alone named too few features). Items that may overlap: fungal infections is an organism class that can co-occur with any site item; necrotic skin ulcers can also count as a skin infection in 33391282's wording; diarrhea, gastrointestinal infections and colitis are distinct but often reported together. Weakest item: autoimmune complications, which 33391282 cites as previously reported but did not see in its own cohort. Meningitis, diarrhea and failure to thrive are supported only by 33391282 Table 1 rows. Features in 23207660 that are LAD-II or LAD-III only were excluded.
